subject: Thinking Machines Inkling 🎙️, OpenAI GPT-Red Security 🛡️, PrismML 27B
intro: Open weights are having a moment. Mira Murati's crew drops Inkling with native audio, vision and text in one clean architecture. No glue code. Meanwhile, Ant's Ring-2.5-1T-Zero trains a trillion-parameter reasoner with zero human annotations and it just... figures things out. The pattern is clear: the open ecosystem is closing the gap fast. And OpenAI quietly ships an AI that attacks its own models 6x more effectively than humans. Security as a feature, not an afterthought. We're here for it.

news.headline: Thinking Machines releases Inkling, an open-weight model that reasons across text, audio, and images
news.body: Thinking Machines Lab just dropped Inkling , their first open-weights model, and it handles text, images, and audio natively in one architecture. No duct-taped components. One model, all three inputs. Here is what makes it interesting to work with: You can fine-tune it today on Tinker, grab the weights on Hugging Face, or just play in the Inkling Playground. An Inkling-Small version is also previewed for lighter workloads.
bullets: 975B total parameters, 41B active per task, so it is big but not slow
1 million token context window , trained on 45 trillion tokens across text, image, audio, and video
Top open-weights audio scores on VoiceBench, MMAU, and AudioMC, it can transcribe, follow spoken instructions, and reason over recordings
Controllable thinking effort , dial reasoning up or down to trade speed for accuracy, reaching the same score with a fraction of the tokens
Apache 2.0 license, download it, modify it, run it on-premises

news.headline: OpenAI's automated red-teaming tool cuts prompt injection failures 6x
news.body: OpenAI just shipped GPT-Red , an AI that attacks its own models to find security holes before you ever use them. Here's the core idea. A prompt injection is when someone sneaks malicious instructions into an AI's input to hijack its behavior. Think of it like tricking a self-driving car by painting fake road signs. In one real test, GPT-Red manipulated an autonomous vending machine agent into lowering prices, ordering discounted inventory, and canceling another customer's order. The clever part is how GPT-Red learns. It uses self-play, where GPT-Red is rewarded for successfully breaking defender models, while those defenders train to resist. This forces GPT-Red to constantly evolve and discover more sophisticated attacks. The results are hard to ignore: This means every model you build on top of OpenAI's stack gets these defenses baked in automatically.
bullets: GPT-Red found success on 84% of attack scenarios vs. 13% for human testers
GPT-5.6 Sol now has 6x fewer failures on the hardest prompt injection benchmark
GPT-Red independently discovered a novel "fake chain of thought" attack class before human researchers

news.headline: PrismML ships open-source 27B model that fits on a phone at 3.9 GB
news.body: A 27B model normally needs 54GB of memory in standard precision. Even a compressed 4-bit version sits around 18GB, too big for a phone or most laptops. So 27B-class AI has always lived in the cloud. Until now. PrismML just released Bonsai 27B , the first 27B model that fits on a phone. It comes in two flavors: It handles images too, so you can feed it screenshots or documents directly on-device. The big unlock: multi-step AI agents that reason, call tools, and loop through tasks can now run fully local. Your private files never leave the device. No cloud round trips. No per-token costs piling up. Both variants are open-source under Apache 2.0 , available now on Hugging Face with llama.cpp and MLX support.
bullets: Ternary (5.9GB) : laptop-ready, retains 95% of full-precision performance across 15 benchmarks including math, coding, and tool use
1-bit (3.9GB) : phone-ready, retains 90% of full-precision, runs at ~10.8 tok/s on iPhone with 672 tokens per 1% battery
